title: Nawaz Sharif convicted in plane hijacking case
description: A special anti-terrorism court convicted former Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif in the 1999 plane-hijacking case linked to his removal. The conviction reinforced military rule under General Pervez Musharraf and shaped political risk perceptions for years.

title: Pakistan joins US-led post-9/11 coalition
description: After the September 11 attacks, Pakistan decided to support the US-led campaign against al-Qaeda and the Taliban. The policy shift brought security cooperation, aid prospects, and elevated geopolitical risk around Afghanistan.
notes: Market-relevant date is first Pakistan trading session after 9/11 decisions; exact announcement cadence varies by outlet.

title: US-led military campaign in Afghanistan begins
description: The US and allies began military operations in Afghanistan against the Taliban and al-Qaeda. Pakistan's role as a frontline state raised security, refugee, and economic-spillover concerns for investors.

title: Musharraf presidential referendum
description: General Pervez Musharraf held a referendum seeking a five-year presidential term. Results were reported as strongly in his favour amid opposition claims of irregularities, extending military-backed civilian transition risk.

title: India-Pakistan military standoff after Kaluchak attack
description: Following the Kaluchak massacre and related attacks, India and Pakistan maintained a large troop mobilisation along the border. War-scare headlines weighed on regional risk appetite and Pakistani equities.
notes: Standoff spanned late 2001–mid 2002; May 2002 used as a peak-tension trading-relevant window.

title: 2002 general elections under Musharraf
description: Pakistan held general elections that returned a fragmented National Assembly and elevated the PML-Q as a pro-Musharraf force. The poll marked a managed transition from pure military rule toward a hybrid civilian setup.

title: Assassination attempt on Musharraf in Rawalpindi
description: A bomb attack targeted President Musharraf's convoy in Rawalpindi. The attempt highlighted domestic terrorism risk and leadership continuity concerns.
notes: A second attempt occurred on 25 Dec 2003.

title: Islamabad SAARC summit and India-Pakistan thaw
description: On the sidelines of the SAARC summit in Islamabad, India and Pakistan agreed to resume a composite dialogue. Improved bilateral atmospherics reduced immediate war-risk premium.

title: Shaukat Aziz becomes prime minister
description: Finance Minister Shaukat Aziz became prime minister after a by-election, reinforcing a technocratic economic team under Musharraf. Continuity of privatisation and growth policies was the market narrative.

title: PTCL privatisation process advances
description: The government advanced privatisation of Pakistan Telecommunication Company Limited, culminating in a major stake sale to Etisalat in 2005–2006. The process was a flagship structural reform and capital-markets signal.
notes: Deal milestones spanned 2005–2006; December 2004 marks active bidding/process phase. Exact daily milestone may vary by source.

title: Muzaffarabad-Srinagar bus service launched
description: India and Pakistan launched the historic Muzaffarabad–Srinagar bus service across the LoC. The confidence-building measure supported a broader peace process narrative.

title: 2005 Kashmir earthquake
description: A magnitude-7.6 earthquake struck northern Pakistan and Azad Kashmir, killing tens of thousands and devastating infrastructure. Reconstruction needs, fiscal strain, and humanitarian disruption affected investor confidence.

title: Etisalat named leading bidder for PTCL stake
description: Etisalat emerged as the leading bidder in the PTCL privatisation, a landmark SOE sale. Completion and payment disputes continued afterward, but the bid itself was a major capital-markets signal.
notes: Exact award announcement day can vary by source within October 2005.

title: US President Bush visits Pakistan
description: US President George W. Bush visited Pakistan amid the war-on-terror partnership. The visit reaffirmed aid and security ties while also spotlighting democracy and nuclear concerns.

title: Killing of Nawab Akbar Bugti
description: Baloch leader Nawab Akbar Bugti was killed during a military operation in Balochistan. The event intensified the Baloch insurgency and raised security and political risk premiums.

title: Chief Justice Iftikhar Chaudhry suspended
description: President Musharraf suspended Chief Justice Iftikhar Muhammad Chaudhry, triggering the lawyers' movement. Prolonged judicial-political confrontation increased institutional uncertainty.

title: Lal Masjid operation in Islamabad
description: Security forces stormed Lal Masjid after a standoff with militants in the capital. The operation was followed by a surge in militant attacks nationwide.

title: Supreme Court restores Chief Justice Chaudhry
description: The Supreme Court reinstated Chief Justice Iftikhar Chaudhry, a landmark win for the lawyers' movement. Institutional confrontation with the executive nonetheless continued into the November emergency.

title: Benazir Bhutto returns; Karachi convoy bombed
description: Former Prime Minister Benazir Bhutto returned from exile and her welcoming procession in Karachi was hit by twin bombings, killing scores. Political violence ahead of elections sharply raised risk premiums.

title: Musharraf declares state of emergency
description: President Musharraf imposed a state of emergency, suspended the constitution, and purged parts of the judiciary. Capital markets faced acute political and institutional uncertainty.

title: Assassination of Benazir Bhutto
description: Benazir Bhutto was assassinated after a campaign rally in Rawalpindi. Nationwide unrest, delayed elections, and political vacuum created a severe confidence shock.

title: 2008 general elections; PPP-led coalition emerges
description: Pakistan held general elections after Bhutto's assassination. The PPP and allies defeated Musharraf's political machine, setting up a transition toward civilian coalition government.

title: Pervez Musharraf resigns as president
description: Facing impeachment pressure from the ruling coalition, President Pervez Musharraf resigned. Markets treated the end of his presidency as a major political regime shift.

title: Asif Ali Zardari elected president
description: Asif Ali Zardari was elected President of Pakistan by the electoral college. The PPP consolidated civilian executive power amid economic stress and security challenges.

title: Marriott Hotel bombing in Islamabad
description: A massive truck bomb devastated the Marriott Hotel in Islamabad, killing dozens. The attack hit the diplomatic and business community in the capital and raised security costs.

title: IMF approves 2008 Stand-By Arrangement
description: The IMF Executive Board approved a Stand-By Arrangement for Pakistan amid a balance-of-payments crisis, FX reserve drain, and global financial turmoil. Conditionality covered fiscal adjustment and monetary tightening.
notes: IMF press release date may be listed as 24 Nov 2008; confirm against IMF archive if precise timestamp needed.

title: Mumbai terror attacks strain India-Pakistan ties
description: Coordinated terrorist attacks in Mumbai killed many civilians and were blamed by India on Pakistan-based militants. Bilateral tensions spiked and peace-process momentum collapsed.

title: Chief Justice restored after long march
description: Under pressure from the lawyers' movement and a PML-N long march, the government restored Chief Justice Iftikhar Chaudhry. The episode resolved an acute political crisis but highlighted coalition fragility.

title: Military offensive in Swat (Second Battle of Swat)
description: Pakistan launched a major offensive against Taliban militants in Swat after the collapse of a peace deal. Displacement and security costs weighed on confidence even as the state reasserted control.
notes: Offensive intensified in May 2009; start date approximate to early May operations.

title: Kerry-Lugar-Berman Act signed
description: The US Enhanced Partnership with Pakistan Act authorised multi-year civilian assistance. Domestic political controversy over perceived sovereignty conditions accompanied the aid commitment.

title: 18th Amendment enacted
description: Pakistan enacted the 18th Constitutional Amendment, devolving powers to provinces and curtailing presidential authority. Markets viewed it as a structural political settlement with fiscal federalism implications.

title: 2010 Pakistan super floods intensify
description: Catastrophic monsoon flooding submerged large parts of Pakistan, affecting roughly 20 million people and damaging crops and infrastructure. Fiscal and growth outlooks deteriorated sharply.
notes: Flood peak spanned late July–August 2010; 29 Jul used as a representative trading-relevant intensification date.

title: NATO tanker attacks and Afghan supply-route risk
description: Militant attacks on NATO supply convoys through Pakistan intensified debates over transit routes to Afghanistan. Security and bilateral friction with Western partners affected risk perceptions.
notes: Attacks were recurrent in 2010; October date is representative, not a unique single incident.

title: Post-flood reconstruction and fiscal strain
description: By late 2010, reconstruction needs from the super floods strained public finances and growth. Donor conferences and domestic revenue measures shaped the macro outlook.
source: Ministry of Finance / World Bank / Dawn
notes: Composite aftermath theme; December representative of reconstruction financing phase.

title: Raymond Davis incident in Lahore
description: US contractor Raymond Davis shot two men in Lahore, triggering a major diplomatic crisis. The episode strained US-Pakistan ties and dominated political attention.

title: Osama bin Laden killed in Abbottabad
description: US special forces killed Osama bin Laden in a compound in Abbottabad without prior Pakistani operational coordination publicly acknowledged. The raid created a profound sovereignty and alliance crisis.
notes: Raid occurred late 1 May US time / early 2 May Pakistan time.

title: PNS Mehran naval base attack in Karachi
description: Taliban militants attacked PNS Mehran in Karachi, destroying aircraft and killing personnel. The assault underscored militant reach against high-value military assets in an economic hub.

title: Salala checkpoint attack; NATO routes closed
description: NATO/ISAF airstrikes killed Pakistani soldiers at the Salala checkpoint near the Afghan border. Pakistan closed NATO supply routes and vacated the Shamsi airbase, deepening the alliance rupture.

title: Memogate scandal intensifies civil-military tension
description: The Memogate controversy over an alleged memo seeking US help against the military deepened civil-military distrust. Political risk rose around the PPP government and Ambassador Haqqani.
notes: Scandal spanned late 2011–2012; early January used as a representative intensification window.

title: Supreme Court disqualifies PM Yousaf Raza Gilani
description: The Supreme Court convicted and effectively disqualified Prime Minister Yousaf Raza Gilani for contempt related to the Swiss letter/NRO issue. Leadership uncertainty followed until a successor was elected.

title: Pakistan reopens NATO supply routes
description: After months of closure following Salala, Pakistan reopened NATO ground supply routes to Afghanistan following US apologies and negotiations. The move eased a major bilateral freeze.

title: Malala Yousafzai shot by Taliban in Swat
description: Taliban gunmen shot education activist Malala Yousafzai in Mingora. The attack drew global condemnation and spotlighted extremism's social and reputational costs.
notes: Market severity prior moderate; event is socially and reputationally major.

title: Quetta Hazara bombings deepen sectarian crisis
description: Deadly bombings targeting Hazara Shia communities in Quetta triggered protests and national outrage. Sectarian violence risk featured prominently in early-2013 security assessments.
notes: Multiple Quetta attacks in early 2013; 10 Jan is a major documented episode.

title: 2013 general elections; PML-N wins majority
description: Pakistan held general elections marking the first democratic transition between civilian governments. PML-N won a National Assembly majority and Nawaz Sharif returned as prime minister.

title: IMF approves 2013 Extended Fund Facility
description: The IMF approved a three-year Extended Fund Facility for Pakistan to rebuild reserves and support fiscal/energy reforms under the new PML-N government. Markets watched FX and subsidy conditionality closely.

title: Church bombing in Peshawar
description: Twin suicide bombings at All Saints Church in Peshawar killed dozens of worshippers. The attack underscored persistent terrorism risk despite military operations.

title: Karachi airport attack
description: Militants attacked Jinnah International Airport in Karachi, killing security personnel and civilians and disrupting aviation. The assault helped precipitate Operation Zarb-e-Azb.

title: Operation Zarb-e-Azb launched in North Waziristan
description: The military launched Operation Zarb-e-Azb against militant sanctuaries in North Waziristan after the Karachi airport attack. Markets weighed security gains against displacement and fiscal costs.

title: PTI-PAT Islamabad sit-in (Azadi March)
description: PTI and Pakistan Awami Tehreek began prolonged sit-ins in Islamabad demanding Nawaz Sharif's resignation over alleged 2013 election rigging. Political paralysis and protest violence unsettled markets.

title: Army Public School massacre in Peshawar
description: Tehrik-i-Taliban Pakistan militants attacked Army Public School in Peshawar, killing around 150 people, mostly children. The atrocity led to the National Action Plan and a hardline anti-terror consensus.

title: 21st Amendment establishes military courts
description: Parliament passed the 21st Constitutional Amendment enabling military courts for terrorism cases under the National Action Plan. The reform was contentious for civil liberties but framed as a security response after APS.

title: Youhanabad church attacks in Lahore
description: Suicide bombings outside churches in Youhanabad, Lahore, killed and injured many worshippers and sparked communal unrest. Security and social cohesion risks resurfaced in Punjab's commercial hub.

title: Xi Jinping visit; CPEC agreements signed
description: Chinese President Xi Jinping visited Islamabad and signed a package of CPEC energy and infrastructure agreements. Markets treated CPEC as a multi-year investment and FX/financing narrative.

title: Paris Agreement era climate diplomacy (Pakistan joins global deal)
description: Pakistan participated in the Paris climate agreement process concluding in December 2015. Longer-term implications concerned climate vulnerability, energy transition, and disaster-finance narratives.
notes: Low near-term equity severity; included for macro-theme completeness. Adoption/signature timing differs from entry-into-force.

title: Pathankot airbase attack
description: Militants attacked India's Pathankot airbase shortly after a high-level bilateral thaw attempt. The incident set back India-Pakistan diplomacy and raised security headlines.

title: Gulshan-e-Iqbal Park bombing in Lahore
description: A suicide bombing in Lahore's Gulshan-e-Iqbal Park on Easter Sunday killed dozens, many of them women and children. The attack shocked markets and prompted security crackdowns.

title: Panama Papers name Nawaz Sharif family
description: The Panama Papers leak reported offshore companies linked to the family of Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif. Political and judicial fallout escalated into a Supreme Court case that later removed him from office.

title: Power-sector circular debt remains elevated
description: Policy and media reporting through mid-2016 highlighted persistently large power-sector circular debt despite prior IMF-era tariff and subsidy reforms. Energy-sector fiscal risk remained a structural market theme.
notes: Not a single announcement day; August 2016 used as a representative reporting window. Severity is structural, not event-spike.

title: Uri attack and subsequent India-Pakistan crisis
description: An attack on an Indian Army base in Uri raised Kashmir tensions. India later announced 'surgical strikes,' and bilateral rhetoric hardened, elevating geopolitical risk for Pakistani assets.
notes: Surgical strikes announced by India on 29 Sep 2016; Uri attack on 18 Sep is the initiating event.

title: 2017 population census operations
description: Pakistan conducted a long-delayed national census with implications for NFC awards, seats, and fiscal federalism. Markets treated it as a medium-term institutional rather than immediate price shock.
notes: Census spanned March–May 2017; mid/late April is representative.

title: Belt and Road / CPEC progress under scrutiny
description: Through mid-2017, Pakistani and Chinese officials publicly reaffirmed CPEC timelines while opposition and media debated debt, transparency, and project pacing. Investor narratives remained CPEC-sensitive.
notes: Diffuse process event; date is representative of mid-2017 CPEC discourse rather than a single treaty signing.

title: Supreme Court disqualifies Nawaz Sharif
description: In the Panama Papers case, the Supreme Court disqualified Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif from office. Leadership succession and PML-N instability followed immediately.

title: Faizabad sit-in ends after agreement
description: A Tehreek-e-Labbaik Pakistan sit-in at Faizabad interchange paralysed Islamabad-Rawalpindi traffic until an agreement with the government. The episode raised questions about state capacity and religious-political pressure.

title: Pakistan placed on FATF grey list
description: FATF added Pakistan to its grey list (jurisdictions under increased monitoring) over AML/CFT deficiencies. Banks, remittances, and correspondent relationships faced heightened compliance scrutiny.
notes: FATF plenary timing late February 2018; some outlets dated announcement 23–24 Feb.

title: PML-N government completes term; caretakers installed
description: The National Assembly completed its term and a caretaker setup was installed ahead of general elections. Markets entered a familiar pre-election policy-pause phase amid external imbalances.
notes: Exact caretaker notification dates may differ by a day; late May 2018 is the transition window.

title: 2018 general elections; PTI emerges largest party
description: General elections produced a PTI-led government with Imran Khan as prime minister-elect amid opposition allegations of military engineering. Policy uncertainty around IMF engagement and FX adjustment rose.

title: Imran Khan sworn in as prime minister
description: Imran Khan took oath as Prime Minister after PTI formed a coalition government. Markets focused on the new team's macroeconomic stabilisation strategy and relations with the IMF and Gulf partners.

title: PKR under sharp depreciation pressure
description: In late 2018 the rupee faced repeated depreciation as reserves fell and the new government debated market-based FX adjustment before an IMF programme. Importers and listed corporates faced cost shocks.
notes: Depreciation was multi-episode through 2018–2019; mid-October used as a representative stress window.

title: Saudi support package negotiations under PTI government
description: The new PTI government pursued Saudi deposits, oil facilities, and investment pledges to bridge financing gaps before/around IMF entry. Gulf bilateral support became a recurrent FX stabiliser narrative.
notes: Multiple visits/packages in late 2018; late October is a representative negotiation window.

title: Pulwama attack
description: A suicide bombing in Pulwama, Indian-administered Kashmir, killed dozens of Indian security personnel. India blamed Pakistan-based Jaish-e-Mohammed, and bilateral escalation risk surged.

title: Balakot airstrike and Pakistan response
description: India conducted airstrikes it said targeted Balakot; Pakistan responded the next day and an Indian pilot was captured then released. Markets priced acute war-scare risk across the crisis week.

title: SBP tightens policy amid inflation and IMF prior actions
description: Ahead of the 2019 IMF programme, the State Bank raised policy rates as inflation accelerated and the FX regime moved toward greater flexibility. Banking and leveraged corporates faced higher funding costs.
notes: Confirm exact MPC date in March 2019 for precise event windows.

title: Staff-level agreement on 2019 IMF EFF
description: Pakistan and the IMF reached a staff-level agreement on a new Extended Fund Facility after FX and fiscal stress. Formal board approval followed in July 2019 with prior actions on rates, FX, and fiscal measures.

title: IMF Executive Board approves 2019 EFF
description: The IMF Executive Board approved a 39-month Extended Fund Facility for Pakistan. The programme anchored monetary tightening, flexible FX, and fiscal consolidation expectations.

title: India revokes Jammu & Kashmir special status
description: India revoked Article 370 special status for Jammu and Kashmir. Pakistan strongly protested, downgraded diplomatic ties, and Kashmir again dominated geopolitical risk headlines.

title: SBP begins aggressive COVID-era rate cuts
description: As the pandemic shock hit, the State Bank of Pakistan started a rapid policy-rate cutting cycle through spring–summer 2020. Liquidity and credit-support measures accompanied monetary easing.
notes: Multiple MPC decisions from March–June 2020; 6 Mar is early-cycle representative date. Verify exact MPC calendar for event studies.

title: COVID-19 lockdowns begin nationwide
description: Pakistan imposed COVID-19 lockdowns and mobility restrictions as cases spread. Markets faced a global risk-off shock plus domestic activity collapse in services and retail.
notes: Provincial lockdown timing varied; late March is the national crisis onset window.

title: IMF Rapid Financing Instrument for COVID response
description: The IMF approved emergency financing under the Rapid Financing Instrument to help Pakistan address the COVID-19 shock. The support aimed to shore up health spending and external buffers.

title: Desert locust outbreak damages crops
description: A severe desert locust outbreak damaged crops across parts of Pakistan in 2019–2020, compounding COVID-era rural stress. Food-price and agricultural-output concerns featured in macro commentary.
source: FAO / Ministry of National Food Security
notes: Outbreak was multi-month; June 2020 is a representative COVID-overlapping window.

title: Pakistan Democratic Movement launched
description: Major opposition parties launched the Pakistan Democratic Movement to challenge the PTI government. Prolonged protest politics increased political noise into 2021.

title: FATF keeps Pakistan on grey list with remaining actions
description: FATF plenaries through 2021 kept Pakistan under increased monitoring while acknowledging progress on the action plan. Grey-list overhang continued to affect banking compliance costs and sentiment.
notes: Multiple 2021 plenaries; February used as a representative monitoring update.

title: French ambassador recall controversy / TLP protests
description: Tehreek-e-Labbaik Pakistan protests over caricatures and French diplomatic ties disrupted parts of Punjab and national politics. Government-TLP negotiations and bans periodically unsettled urban commerce.
notes: TLP protest waves recurred in 2021; early April marks a major flare-up window.

title: FY2022 federal budget under PTI
description: The PTI government presented the FY2022 federal budget amid rebounding growth, rising inflation, and external-account pressures. Tax and energy measures were closely watched by equity investors.

title: Taliban takeover of Kabul
description: The Taliban seized Kabul as the Afghan republic collapsed. Pakistan faced refugee, TTP spillover, trade-route, and diplomatic recognition dilemmas with market-relevant security externalities.

title: Fuel and energy price pressures intensify
description: Rising global oil prices and domestic subsidy/circular-debt constraints forced difficult energy-pricing decisions. Inflation and current-account stress became dominant market themes into late 2021.
notes: Process event across Q3–Q4 2021; October used as representative month.

title: Fuel subsidy policy clash ahead of IMF talks
description: Disputes over fuel subsidies and their fiscal cost intensified before the no-confidence crisis, complicating IMF programme revival. Energy pricing became a political-market flashpoint.
notes: Process dispute across early 2022; late February representative.

title: No-confidence motion filed against Imran Khan
description: Opposition parties filed a no-confidence motion against Prime Minister Imran Khan. Weeks of parliamentary brinkmanship created high political uncertainty for markets.

title: National Assembly deputy speaker rejects no-confidence vote
description: A chaotic National Assembly session saw the no-confidence vote rejected and the Assembly dissolved, prompting Supreme Court intervention. Constitutional crisis headlines dominated markets that week.

title: Imran Khan ousted; Shehbaz Sharif elected PM
description: After the Supreme Court restored the National Assembly process, Imran Khan lost the no-confidence vote and Shehbaz Sharif was elected prime minister. Markets priced coalition policy shifts and IMF re-engagement.

title: Cipher / 'foreign conspiracy' narrative escalates politics
description: PTI's campaign around an alleged diplomatic cipher and foreign conspiracy narrative intensified after the no-confidence vote. Political polarisation and street mobilisation remained elevated.
notes: Ongoing narrative event; late May 2022 used as a representative intensification window around PTI protests.

title: PKR hits record lows amid reserve stress
description: The rupee suffered sharp depreciation in mid-2022 as foreign reserves dwindled and IMF negotiations stalled over energy subsidies and fiscal measures. Import compression and inflation expectations worsened.
notes: Multi-week FX stress; mid-July used as a representative acute window.

title: 2022 monsoon super floods peak
description: Unprecedented monsoon flooding submerged large parts of Sindh and Balochistan, with massive humanitarian and agricultural losses. Growth, fiscal, and inflation outlooks deteriorated further.
notes: Floods spanned June–September; late August captures peak national emergency recognition.

title: IMF board completes 2022 EFF review / tranche
description: After difficult prior actions on fuel prices and fiscal measures, Pakistan secured IMF board approval restoring programme access. The decision temporarily eased default fears.

title: FATF removes Pakistan from grey list
description: FATF announced Pakistan's removal from the grey list after completion of the action plan. Banking and sovereign-risk narratives treated delisting as a medium-term positive.
notes: Plenary announcement widely reported 21 Oct 2022.

title: Assassination attempt on Imran Khan in Wazirabad
description: Gunfire struck Imran Khan's container during a long march in Wazirabad, wounding him and killing supporters. Political violence risk spiked and protest politics intensified.

title: Interbank-open market PKR divergence crisis
description: Severe dollar shortages produced wide gaps between interbank and open-market PKR rates, import restrictions, and default-risk chatter. Equity and corporate earnings confidence weakened.
notes: Stress peaked across Jan–Feb 2023; 25 Jan used as representative acute date.

title: CPEC project security and financing reassessment
description: Attacks on Chinese interests and slower project execution prompted Islamabad and Beijing to emphasise CPEC security and recalibration. China bilateral financing remained critical for external sustainability.
notes: Theme event for early 2023; refine with a specific bilateral visit or attack date for tight windows.

title: Fiscal / IMF prior-action package before SBA
description: Authorities implemented difficult fiscal and FX measures as prior actions for a new IMF programme, including taxation and energy-pricing steps. Near-term growth and inflation trade-offs dominated market debate.
notes: Package unfolded over late March–June 2023; late March marks early public sequencing.

title: Imran Khan arrested; May 9 unrest
description: Imran Khan's arrest from the Islamabad High Court premises triggered nationwide protests and attacks on military and civic installations. Markets faced acute political and security shock.

title: IMF approves Stand-By Arrangement for Pakistan
description: The IMF Executive Board approved a Stand-By Arrangement, unlocking financing and catalysing bilateral support after months of default fears. Equity and FX sentiment improved on the announcement.
notes: Staff-level agreement was earlier in June/July sequencing; board approval widely dated around end-June/early July 2023 depending on release. URL is official IMF release; cross-check exact calendar day for event studies.

title: PTI loses election symbol amid legal crackdown
description: Election and court processes stripped PTI of its electoral symbol while many leaders faced cases after May 9. Political competition ahead of national polls became highly asymmetric.
notes: Legal milestones clustered in mid–late 2023; early August used as representative.

title: Shehbaz Sharif government ends; caretaker setup begins
description: After completing its parliamentary path to elections, the PDM-led government gave way to a caretaker administration. Markets entered a caretaker policy-holding pattern amid IMF programme monitoring.

title: SBP holds ultra-tight policy rate near cycle peak
description: Through late 2023 the State Bank maintained a historically high policy rate to anchor inflation after FX liberalisation. Real-economy and listed-company financing costs remained elevated.
notes: Representative MPC window; confirm exact decision date for event-study windows.

title: 2024 general elections produce fragmented mandate
description: General elections delivered a hung parliament with strong showings by independents backed by PTI alongside PML-N and PPP. Delayed results and controversy over transparency weighed on confidence.

title: Shehbaz Sharif returns as prime minister
description: Shehbaz Sharif was elected prime minister by the new National Assembly at the head of a PML-N–PPP coalition. Continuity on IMF engagement was the core market narrative.

title: Asif Ali Zardari elected president again
description: Asif Ali Zardari won the presidential election, returning to the presidency as part of the post-poll coalition settlement. Markets treated it as political continuity rather than a policy shock.

title: Staff-level agreement on new IMF EFF
description: Pakistan reached a staff-level agreement with the IMF on a new Extended Fund Facility after the Stand-By Arrangement, focusing on fiscal consolidation, SOE reform, and FX market functioning.
notes: Confirm exact IMF press-release date; May 2024 SLA widely reported — verification medium pending exact day match to IMF archive.

title: FY2025 federal budget with IMF-aligned taxation
description: The coalition government presented a federal budget emphasising revenue measures aligned with IMF programme parameters. Equity sectors faced mixed implications from tax and energy pricing changes.

title: IMF Executive Board approves 2024 EFF
description: The IMF Executive Board approved a new Extended Fund Facility for Pakistan, locking in a multi-year reform and financing framework. Sovereign and FX stability expectations improved on the margin.

title: Security incidents and TTP threat remain elevated
description: Through 2024, Pakistan faced renewed TTP and militant violence especially in KP and Balochistan. Persistent security headlines weighed on investment and provincial risk premia.
notes: Composite security theme rather than a single attack; late August used as representative 2024 window.

title: Capital gains / equity market tax debates under IMF
description: Budget and mini-budget discussions in 2024 revisited capital gains and market-related tax measures in the context of IMF revenue goals. Brokerage and investor sentiment often reacted to draft proposals even before final law.
notes: Use a specific Finance Bill clause date for formal event studies; September marks ongoing implementation debate.

title: SOE privatisation push under IMF programme
description: Authorities reiterated privatisation and SOE reform commitments for entities such as loss-making state firms under the IMF framework. Progress remained politically and execution-sensitive for markets.
notes: Process milestone; not a completed mega-transaction on this date.

title: SBP easing cycle continues into 2025
description: With inflation moderating from extreme highs, the State Bank continued a policy-rate cutting cycle into early 2025. Markets debated growth recovery versus external-account risks under the IMF programme.
notes: Exact MPC dates should be matched to SBP calendar for event studies; mid-January is a representative early-2025 easing window.

title: Energy circular debt and tariff adjustments persist
description: Energy circular debt and periodic tariff/fuel-price adjustments remained a structural social and industrial cost shock into 2025. Household and SME stress fed into political and market narratives.
notes: Structural theme dated to a representative month; pair with a specific OGRA/ECC decision for precise event studies.

title: IMF programme reviews remain market anchor
description: IMF review missions and board considerations continued to anchor Pakistan's 2025 macroeconomic narrative on fiscal targets, FX market depth, and energy reforms. Tranche timing stayed a key sentiment driver.
source: International Monetary Fund / Ministry of Finance
notes: Composite review process for early 2025; pin exact board dates from IMF releases for research use.

title: Kashmir / India-Pakistan diplomatic tensions recur
description: Periodic India-Pakistan diplomatic and LoC tensions continued to inject geopolitical risk premia into Pakistani assets in 2025. Investor focus remained on escalation risk rather than durable dialogue.
notes: Representative 2025 tension window; not a claim of a unique named crisis day. Refine with a specific documented incident before event-study use.

title: FY2026 federal budget under IMF constraints
description: The FY2026 budget exercise remained constrained by IMF revenue and primary-balance targets. Sectoral tax changes and energy circular-debt measures were central to equity-market interpretation.
notes: Budget presentation day should be confirmed against Finance Division release; early/mid-June is the conventional window.

title: SECP/PSX regulatory and listing reform agenda
description: Through 2025, SECP and PSX continued incremental capital-market reforms on disclosure, listing, and investor protection under the broader stabilisation backdrop. Direct index impact is usually gradual rather than jump-like.
notes: Process theme; replace with a specific circular date when using for tight event windows.
